sources.entry: pytorch - Tensors and dynamic neural networks in Python with strong GPU acceleration.

summary.one_liner: PyTorch is a Python package for tensor computation with GPU acceleration and a tape-based autograd system for building deep neural networks.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a NumPy-like Tensor library that can run on CPU or GPU, with a wide set of tensor routines (slicing, indexing, math, linear algebra, reductions). Includes torch.autograd for automatic differentiation over tensor operations, torch.nn for building neural networks, torch.multiprocessing for sharing tensors across processes, and torch.utils such as DataLoader. The README describes dynamic, imperative execution where networks can be changed freely as code runs, and says layers can be written in Python or in C/C++ via an extension API. Installation is covered via Conda or pip binaries, from source (CPU, CUDA, ROCm, Intel GPU, macOS, Windows), and via Docker images.
use_cases: build and train deep neural networks
building PyTorch from source with CUDA or ROCm
how_to_run: pip install --group dev  (run from the cloned pytorch directory)
git submodule sync && git submodule update --init --recursive
notable: Tape-based reverse-mode autograd that lets network behavior change at runtime without rebuilding the graph
Imperative execution with stack traces pointing to the user's code
Custom GPU memory allocators for memory efficiency
C/C++ extension API described as requiring minimal boilerplate
Pre-built Docker images on Docker Hub with CUDA and cuDNN support
caveats: Building from source needs 10 GB+ disk space and 30-60 minutes for the initial build
Source builds require a C++20 compiler; gcc 11.3 or newer on Linux
ROCm support is Linux-only; Intel GPU support is Linux and Windows
Jetson wheels are maintained by individual contributors and require JetPack 4.2+
